content.text:
The image shows five separate carbon monoxide units and one Fe atom, with no bonds between them. Each CO is drawn as C with a lone pair, a triple bond (shown as two lines plus a dash) and O. This is iron pentacarbonyl drawn as disconnected fragments.

Each CO is drawn as [C]#O with a lone pair on carbon, which corresponds to the neutral carbon monoxide form [C-]#[O+]. Written as a disconnected-component SMILES, the drawing is five CO fragments plus Fe:

[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[Fe]

The charges are not drawn in the image. Writing the carbons as C with a lone pair and a triple bond to O gives `[C]#O`, or simply `C#O` with implicit hydrogens, which would be wrong. I use the charge-separated form because it is the valid way to represent CO.

SMILES: [C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[Fe]
